column11: comparator estimate: Merck's charge as mrk_calderasib.csv carries it, word for word, so growth_investment reads the same restatements off it. derived: Merck generated $39,599mm of free cash flow on $189,294mm of revenue over 2023, 2024 and 2025, a 20.92% margin, against the 29.5% its cost of sales, SG&A and R&D leave. Solved so the modelled book reproduces that margin rather than assumed from one line's cost structure: the alliance rows carry no cost of sales and Animal Health carries its own, so a ratio taken off a single product does not reconcile the company. Restated before interest: MRK paid $3,700mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 1.95% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 12.10% to 10.14%. Restated at replacement capex: MRK spent $11,347mm on plant over 2023 to 2025 against $6,977mm of plant depreciation, 2.31% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge falls from 10.14% to 7.48%. Restated without one-off cash: MRK's free cash flow over 2023 to 2025 carried $8,300mm of deal payments in operating cash flow, capital allocation whose assets the book values separately; $572mm of legal settlements; $1,200mm of US transition tax (2025 instalment 1,200mm). None recurs, so the charge falls from 7.48% to 2.06%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 MRK's cash flow statement shows receivables up $2,482mm, inventories up $2,831mm, payables down $88mm, a working capital build of $5,401mm, 2.85% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from 2.06% to -1.23%. Rebuilt on the book's own ratios on 0.3610 of the revenue they are struck on, against 0.3746 the filings leave as cash over 2023 to 2025 (free cash flow before interest, at replacement capex, without one-off cash and without working capital build), so the charge is -1.3576%.
